react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: active remodelling of the sex-steroid metabolome. RaMP-DB ORA (multi-DB) ranked 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (KEGG:map00150 / SMPDB:SMP00068) as its #1 hit with FDR = 5.74e-15, with a 1429-fold enrichment — five of the seven input metabolites mapped (dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, and estradiol). The same pathway concept appeared as mummichog's top-ranked m/z-direct hit (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p = 8.40e-05) with an extraordinary 11/11 compound overlap, and as MetaboAnalystR PSEA's sole KEGG hit (hsa00140, p = 8.39e-06) also spanning all five sex steroids. The three non-steroid inputs — butanone, sulindac, and one unresolved KEGG compound — did not contribute to any steroid pathway, consistent with their unrelated chemical structures. Across paradigms, testosterone (KEGG:C00535), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), DHEA (KEGG:C01227), estradiol (KEGG:C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917) form the driver-metabolite set, all canonical intermediates of the CYP17A1/CYP19A1/AKR1C axis in steroidogenesis. Butanone (C4 ketone) and the NSAID sulindac are pharmacologically consistent with CYP/COX inhibition contexts but fall outside the core steroid biosynthesis roster. The cross-paradigm consensus — ORA at FDR 10^-15 level, network m/z at p = 8.4e-05, KEGG PSEA at p = 8.4e-06 — is unambiguous and biologically coherent.
